items.name: Exp. Share
items.description: A held item that grants 50% experience to the holder without participating in battle (Gens 2-5), or key item sharing exp with all party members (Gens 6-9).

Red.location: Route 15 (East Guard House 2F)
Red.instructions: Talk to Professor Oak's Aide on 2F of the gatehouse connecting Route 15 and Fuchsia City. Requires having caught at least 50 different Pokémon species.
Red.prerequisites: 50 Pokémon caught in Pokédex

Blue.location: Route 15 (East Guard House 2F)
Blue.instructions: Talk to Professor Oak's Aide on 2F of the gatehouse connecting Route 15 and Fuchsia City. Requires having caught at least 50 different Pokémon species.
Blue.prerequisites: 50 Pokémon caught in Pokédex

Yellow.location: Route 15 (East Guard House 2F)
Yellow.instructions: Talk to Professor Oak's Aide on 2F of the gatehouse connecting Route 15 and Fuchsia City. Requires having caught at least 50 different Pokémon species.
Yellow.prerequisites: 50 Pokémon caught in Pokédex

Gold.location: Route 30 (Mr. Pokémon's House)
Gold.instructions: Defeat or catch the Red Gyarados at the Lake of Rage to obtain the Red Scale. Bring the Red Scale to Mr. Pokémon's House north of Cherrygrove on Route 30 to trade for the Exp. Share.
Gold.prerequisites: Red Scale from Lake of Rage Red Gyarados

Silver.location: Route 30 (Mr. Pokémon's House)
Silver.instructions: Defeat or catch the Red Gyarados at the Lake of Rage to obtain the Red Scale. Bring the Red Scale to Mr. Pokémon's House north of Cherrygrove on Route 30 to trade for the Exp. Share.
Silver.prerequisites: Red Scale from Lake of Rage Red Gyarados

Crystal.location: Route 30 (Mr. Pokémon's House)
Crystal.instructions: Defeat or catch the Red Gyarados at the Lake of Rage to obtain the Red Scale. Bring the Red Scale to Mr. Pokémon's House north of Cherrygrove on Route 30 to trade for the Exp. Share.
Crystal.prerequisites: Red Scale from Lake of Rage Red Gyarados

HeartGold.instructions: Defeat or catch the Red Gyarados at the Lake of Rage to obtain the Red Scale. Take it to Mr. Pokémon on Route 30 to trade for the Exp. Share. A second Exp. Share is won in the Goldenrod Radio Lottery (match 3 digits).
HeartGold.prerequisites: Red Scale from Lake of Rage Red Gyarados

SoulSilver.location: Route 30 (Mr. Pokémon's House)
SoulSilver.instructions: Defeat or catch the Red Gyarados at the Lake of Rage to obtain the Red Scale. Take it to Mr. Pokémon on Route 30 to trade for the Exp. Share. A second Exp. Share is won in the Goldenrod Radio Lottery (match 3 digits).
SoulSilver.prerequisites: Red Scale from Lake of Rage Red Gyarados

Ruby.instructions: Deliver the Letter to Steven Stone in Granite Cave on Dewford Island. Return to Rustboro City and talk to Devon President Mr. Stone on the 3rd floor of the headquarters to receive the Exp. Share as a reward.
Ruby.prerequisites: Deliver Letter to Steven Stone in Granite Cave

Sapphire.location: Rustboro City (Devon Corporation 3F)
Sapphire.instructions: Deliver the Letter to Steven Stone in Granite Cave on Dewford Island. Return to Rustboro City and talk to Devon President Mr. Stone on the 3rd floor of the headquarters to receive the Exp. Share as a reward.
Sapphire.prerequisites: Deliver Letter to Steven Stone in Granite Cave

Emerald.instructions: Deliver the Letter to Steven Stone in Granite Cave on Dewford Island. Return to Rustboro City and talk to Devon President Mr. Stone on the 3rd floor of the headquarters to receive the Exp. Share as a reward.
Emerald.prerequisites: Deliver Letter to Steven Stone in Granite Cave

FireRed.instructions: Talk to Professor Oak's Aide on 2F of the gatehouse connecting Route 15 and Fuchsia City. Requires catching 50 different Pokémon species.

LeafGreen.location: Route 15 (East Gatehouse 2F)
LeafGreen.instructions: Talk to Professor Oak's Aide on 2F of the gatehouse connecting Route 15 and Fuchsia City. Requires catching 50 different Pokémon species.
LeafGreen.prerequisites: 50 Pokémon caught in Pokédex

Diamond.instructions: After seeing at least 35 Pokémon species, speak to Dawn's/Lucas's father (Professor Rowan's assistant) in the gatehouse between Eterna City and Cycling Road (Route 206).
Diamond.prerequisites: Seen 35 Pokémon in Sinnoh Pokédex

Pearl.instructions: After seeing at least 35 Pokémon species, speak to Dawn's/Lucas's father (Professor Rowan's assistant) in the gatehouse between Eterna City and Cycling Road (Route 206).
Pearl.prerequisites: Seen 35 Pokémon in Sinnoh Pokédex

Platinum.instructions: After seeing at least 35 Pokémon species, speak to Dawn's/Lucas's father in the gatehouse south of Eterna City leading to Route 206.
Platinum.prerequisites: Seen 35 Pokémon in Sinnoh Pokédex

Black.instructions: Defeat the Janitor (Cleaner Geoff) on the 55th floor of the Battle Company building in Castelia City. A second Exp. Share is gifted by the Pokémon Fan Club Chairman in Icirrus City if you show a Pokémon that gained 25-49 levels.
Black.prerequisites: Defeat Cleaner Geoff in Battle Company

White.instructions: Defeat the Janitor (Cleaner Geoff) on the 55th floor of the Battle Company building in Castelia City. A second Exp. Share is gifted by the Pokémon Fan Club Chairman in Icirrus City.
White.prerequisites: Defeat Cleaner Geoff in Battle Company

Scarlet.location: Built-in Party Mechanic
Scarlet.instructions: In Pokémon Scarlet, Exp. Share is an integrated system feature that is active automatically from the start of the adventure, distributing experience points to all party members after every battle and catch.
Scarlet.prerequisites: Automatic Core System

Violet.location: Built-in Party Mechanic
Violet.instructions: In Pokémon Violet, Exp. Share is an integrated system feature that is active automatically from the start of the adventure, distributing experience points to all party members after every battle and catch.

items.name: Bicycle
items.description: Increases travel speed significantly and unlocks cycling road bridges.

Red.location: Cerulean City (Miracle Cycle)
Red.instructions: Visit the Pokémon Fan Club in Vermilion City and listen to the Chairman talk about his Rapidash to receive the Bike Voucher. Take the voucher to Miracle Cycle in Cerulean City to redeem the Bicycle for free (normally 1,000,000 Pokédollars).
Red.prerequisites: Bike Voucher from Vermilion Pokémon Fan Club

Blue.location: Cerulean City (Miracle Cycle)
Blue.instructions: Visit the Pokémon Fan Club in Vermilion City and listen to the Chairman to receive the Bike Voucher. Redeem it at Miracle Cycle in Cerulean City.
Blue.prerequisites: Bike Voucher from Vermilion Pokémon Fan Club

Yellow.location: Cerulean City (Miracle Cycle)
Yellow.instructions: Obtain the Bike Voucher from the Fan Club Chairman in Vermilion City and trade it for the Bicycle at the shop in Cerulean City.
Yellow.prerequisites: Bike Voucher from Vermilion Pokémon Fan Club

FireRed.instructions: Speak to the Pokémon Fan Club Chairman in Vermilion City. Listen to his entire speech to receive the Bike Voucher, then redeem it at the Bike Shop in Cerulean City.
FireRed.prerequisites: Bike Voucher from Vermilion Pokémon Fan Club

LeafGreen.location: Cerulean City (Miracle Cycle)
LeafGreen.instructions: Speak to the Pokémon Fan Club Chairman in Vermilion City. Listen to his speech to receive the Bike Voucher, then redeem it at Miracle Cycle in Cerulean City.
LeafGreen.prerequisites: Bike Voucher from Vermilion Pokémon Fan Club

Gold.location: Goldenrod City (Miracle Cycle Shop)
Gold.instructions: Visit the Miracle Cycle shop in southeast Goldenrod City. The owner has zero customers and will lend you a Bicycle for free to advertise his shop. After riding it for a while, he calls you on the Pokégear and lets you keep it permanently.
Gold.prerequisites: Reach Goldenrod City

Silver.location: Goldenrod City (Miracle Cycle Shop)
Silver.instructions: Visit the Miracle Cycle shop in southeast Goldenrod City. The owner gives you a free Bicycle as a loaner to promote his shop. After riding it around Johto, he will call and let you keep it.
Silver.prerequisites: Reach Goldenrod City

HeartGold.instructions: Visit the Bike Shop in southeastern Goldenrod City. The owner will give you a Bicycle for promotional use. After riding it for a short time, he will call and gift it to you permanently.

SoulSilver.location: Goldenrod City (Bike Shop)
SoulSilver.instructions: Visit the Bike Shop in southeastern Goldenrod City. The owner gives you a loaner Bicycle. Keep riding it, and he will call via Pokégear to gift it permanently.
SoulSilver.prerequisites: Reach Goldenrod City

Ruby.instructions: Visit Rydel's Cycles in Mauville City. Rydel will offer you a choice between the Mach Bike (high speed, climb steep muddy slopes) or the Acro Bike (bunny hops, wheelies, crossing rail tracks). You can return to Rydel at any time to switch models.
Ruby.prerequisites: Reach Mauville City

Sapphire.location: Mauville City (Rydel's Cycles)
Sapphire.instructions: Visit Rydel's Cycles in Mauville City. Rydel gives you a free choice between the Mach Bike or the Acro Bike, with free swapping at his shop at any time.
Sapphire.prerequisites: Reach Mauville City

Emerald.instructions: Visit Rydel's Cycles in Mauville City to choose the Mach Bike (speed/mud slopes) or the Acro Bike (rail jumps/hopping). In Emerald, after speaking to specific cyclists across Hoenn, you can even obtain both bikes simultaneously!

Diamond.instructions: Rescue the shop owner Rad Rickshaw from Team Galactic's Eterna Building (defeat Commander Jupiter). Visit his shop in Eterna City afterwards and he will gift you a Bicycle with 3rd and 4th gear speed switching.
Diamond.prerequisites: Defeat Jupiter in Team Galactic Eterna Building

Pearl.instructions: Rescue Rad Rickshaw from Team Galactic Building, then visit his shop in Eterna City to receive your multi-gear Bicycle.
Pearl.prerequisites: Defeat Jupiter in Team Galactic Eterna Building

Platinum.instructions: Clear Team Galactic Eterna Building and defeat Jupiter to rescue Rad Rickshaw. Visit his shop to collect your Bicycle.
Platinum.prerequisites: Defeat Jupiter in Team Galactic Eterna Building

items.name: HM03 Surf
items.description: Powerful 90 BP Water-type move that allows riding across ocean routes, lakes, and rivers.

Red.location: Fuchsia City (Safari Zone Area 4 - Secret House)
Red.instructions: Enter the Safari Zone in Fuchsia City (500 Pokédollars). Navigate through Area 1, Area 2, and Area 3 to reach Area 4 (Deep Safari Zone). Enter the Secret House and talk to the attendant to receive HM03 Surf.
Red.prerequisites: Soul Badge from Koga to use outside battle

Blue.location: Fuchsia City (Safari Zone Area 4 - Secret House)
Blue.instructions: Navigate to the Secret House in Deep Safari Zone (Area 4) in Fuchsia City to receive HM03 Surf.
Blue.prerequisites: Soul Badge from Koga to use outside battle

Yellow.location: Fuchsia City (Safari Zone Area 4 - Secret House)
Yellow.instructions: Reach the Secret House in Area 4 of the Fuchsia Safari Zone before running out of 500 steps to claim HM03 Surf.
Yellow.prerequisites: Soul Badge from Koga to use outside battle

FireRed.location: Fuchsia City (Safari Zone Area 4 - Secret House)
FireRed.instructions: Traverse the Safari Zone to Area 4 and speak to the attendant in the Secret House to receive HM03 Surf. Also collect the Gold Teeth nearby for Strength HM04.
FireRed.prerequisites: Soul Badge from Koga to use outside battle

LeafGreen.location: Fuchsia City (Safari Zone Area 4 - Secret House)
LeafGreen.instructions: Reach the Secret House in Area 4 of the Safari Zone to receive HM03 Surf.
LeafGreen.prerequisites: Soul Badge from Koga to use outside battle

Gold.location: Ecruteak City (Dance Theater)
Gold.instructions: Defeat all 5 Kimono Girls on stage in the Ecruteak City Dance Theater. After winning all 5 battles, speak to the gentleman in the audience who will reward you with HM03 Surf.
Gold.prerequisites: Fog Badge from Morty to use outside battle

Silver.location: Ecruteak City (Dance Theater)
Silver.instructions: Defeat all 5 Kimono Girls in the Ecruteak Dance Theater. Speak to the gentleman on the main floor to receive HM03 Surf.
Silver.prerequisites: Fog Badge from Morty to use outside battle

Crystal.location: Ecruteak City (Dance Theater)
Crystal.instructions: Defeat all 5 Kimono Girls in the Ecruteak Dance Theater and talk to the spectator to receive HM03 Surf.
Crystal.prerequisites: Fog Badge from Morty to use outside battle

HeartGold.instructions: Defeat Team Rocket Grunt on stage at the Dance Theater in Ecruteak City. The patron in the audience will give you HM03 Surf.
HeartGold.prerequisites: Fog Badge from Morty to use outside battle

SoulSilver.location: Ecruteak City (Dance Theater)
SoulSilver.instructions: Defeat the Team Rocket Grunt on stage in the Ecruteak Dance Theater to receive HM03 Surf from the patron.
SoulSilver.prerequisites: Fog Badge from Morty to use outside battle

Ruby.instructions: Defeat your father Gym Leader Norman at the Petalburg Gym to earn the Balance Badge. Afterwards, visit Wally's house to the left of the Gym; Wally's father will reward you with HM03 Surf.
Ruby.prerequisites: Balance Badge from Norman in Petalburg Gym

Sapphire.location: Petalburg City (Wally's House)
Sapphire.instructions: Defeat Norman at the Petalburg Gym for the Balance Badge, then visit Wally's father next door to receive HM03 Surf.
Sapphire.prerequisites: Balance Badge from Norman in Petalburg Gym

Emerald.instructions: Defeat your father Norman at the Petalburg Gym. Exit the gym and enter Wally's house on the west side of town to receive HM03 Surf from Wally's father.
Emerald.prerequisites: Balance Badge from Norman in Petalburg Gym

Diamond.instructions: Defeat the Team Galactic Grunt threatening the town ruins in Celestic Town. Enter the shrine cave, inspect the wall paintings, and Cynthia's grandmother will give you HM03 Surf.
Diamond.prerequisites: Fen Badge from Crasher Wake to use outside battle

Pearl.instructions: Defeat the Team Galactic Grunt in Celestic Town. Cynthia's grandmother will reward you with HM03 Surf inside the shrine.
Pearl.prerequisites: Fen Badge from Crasher Wake to use outside battle

Platinum.instructions: Defeat Galactic Boss Cyrus inside the Celestic Town shrine cave, then speak to Cynthia's grandmother to receive HM03 Surf.
Platinum.prerequisites: Relic Badge from Fantina to use outside battle

items.name: Leftovers
items.description: Gradually restores 1/16th of the holder's maximum HP at the end of every turn.

Red.location: Route 12 & Route 16 (Under Sleeping Snorlax)
Red.instructions: Wake up and capture or defeat the wild Snorlax on Route 12 or Route 16 using the Poké Flute. Stand on the exact tile where Snorlax was sleeping and use the Itemfinder to uncover Leftovers.
Red.prerequisites: Poké Flute, Itemfinder

Blue.location: Route 12 & Route 16 (Under Sleeping Snorlax)
Blue.instructions: Use the Itemfinder on the ground tile where Snorlax was sleeping on Route 12 or Route 16.
Blue.prerequisites: Poké Flute, Itemfinder

Yellow.location: Route 12 & Route 16 (Under Sleeping Snorlax)
Yellow.instructions: Use the Itemfinder on the ground tile where Snorlax was sleeping on Route 12 or Route 16.
Yellow.prerequisites: Poké Flute, Itemfinder

FireRed.instructions: After clearing the Snorlax on Route 12 or Route 16 with the Poké Flute, stand directly on the exact spot Snorlax rested and use the Itemfinder to dig up Leftovers.

LeafGreen.location: Route 12 & Route 16 (Under Sleeping Snorlax)
LeafGreen.instructions: Use Itemfinder on the spot where Snorlax was sleeping on Route 12 or Route 16.
LeafGreen.prerequisites: Poké Flute, Itemfinder

Gold.location: Celadon City Restaurant / Wild Snorlax
Gold.instructions:
1. Check the trash can in the bottom-left corner of the Celadon City Restaurant.
2. Catch the wild Snorlax blocking Diglett's Cave on Route 11 (it holds Leftovers).
3. Trade wild Clefairy from Gen 1 holding Leftovers.
Gold.prerequisites: Reach Kanto / EXPN Card for Snorlax

Silver.location: Celadon City Restaurant / Wild Snorlax
Silver.instructions: Inspect the trash can in the Celadon Restaurant in Kanto, or catch the Route 11 wild Snorlax holding Leftovers.
Silver.prerequisites: Reach Kanto

HeartGold.instructions: Search the trash can in the Celadon City Restaurant, catch the wild Snorlax on Route 11, or find with high-level Pickup ability Pokémon (Lv. 81-100, 1% chance).

SoulSilver.location: Celadon Restaurant / Wild Snorlax / Pickup
SoulSilver.instructions: Search the trash can in Celadon Restaurant or catch the Route 11 wild Snorlax.
SoulSilver.prerequisites: Reach Kanto

Ruby.instructions:
1. Inside the S.S. Tidal ferry (connecting Slateport and Lilycove), inspect the trash can in the lower galley kitchen.
2. Purchase at the Battle Tower for 48 Battle Points (BP).
3. Picked up by high-level Pokémon with the Pickup ability.
Ruby.prerequisites: Post-game S.S. Tidal ticket from Norman

Sapphire.location: S.S. Tidal / Battle Tower
Sapphire.instructions: Inspect the trash can in the kitchen of the S.S. Tidal ferry, or purchase at the Battle Tower for 48 BP.
Sapphire.prerequisites: Post-game S.S. Tidal ticket

Emerald.instructions:
1. Inspect the trash can in the storage kitchen of the S.S. Tidal.
2. Exchange 48 Battle Points (BP) at the Battle Frontier Exchange Service Corner.
3. Pickup ability on Pokémon Lv. 81-100.
Emerald.prerequisites: Defeat Elite Four for S.S. Ticket

Scarlet.location: Cascarrafa (Delibird Presents)
Scarlet.instructions: Purchasable at the Delibird Presents shop in Cascarrafa for 20,000 Pokédollars after earning 4 Gym Badges. Also found lying as a glowing item behind a food stall in Medali.
Scarlet.prerequisites: 20,000 Pokédollars (Cascarrafa Delibird Presents)

Violet.location: Cascarrafa (Delibird Presents)
Violet.instructions: Purchasable at the Delibird Presents shop in Cascarrafa for 20,000 Pokédollars, or found behind a street eatery in Medali.

items.name: Running Shoes
items.description: Allows the player to dash by holding the B button.

Ruby.instructions: Given by your Mom outside your home in Littleroot Town after walking with Professor Birch, or outside Petalburg City.
Ruby.prerequisites: Receive first Pokémon from Professor Birch

Sapphire.location: Petalburg City
Sapphire.instructions: Given by your Mom after receiving your starter Pokémon.
Sapphire.prerequisites: Receive starter Pokémon

Emerald.instructions: Given by your Mom right as you leave Littleroot Town after delivering Birch's Parcel.

FireRed.instructions: Professor Oak's Aide stops you in the gatehouse east of Pewter City after defeating Gym Leader Brock and delivers the Running Shoes from your Mom.

LeafGreen.location: Pewter City (East Gate to Route 3)
LeafGreen.instructions: Oak's Aide gifts you Running Shoes from your Mom after beating Brock.
LeafGreen.prerequisites: Boulder Badge from Brock

HeartGold.instructions: The Guide Gent in Cherrygrove City gives you the Running Shoes after taking you on a tour of town. You can toggle running permanently on the Touch Screen!

SoulSilver.location: Cherrygrove City
SoulSilver.instructions: Received from the Guide Gent in Cherrygrove City.
SoulSilver.prerequisites: Complete Guide Gent tour

Diamond.instructions: Given by your rival or Mom in the gatehouse entering Oreburgh City.
Diamond.prerequisites: Arrive in Oreburgh City

Pearl.instructions: Given in the gatehouse entering Oreburgh City.
Pearl.prerequisites: Arrive in Oreburgh City

Platinum.instructions: Given in the gatehouse entering Oreburgh City.
Platinum.prerequisites: Arrive in Oreburgh City

items.name: Fishing Rods (Old, Good, Super)
items.description: Equipment used to reel in wild Water-type Pokémon from rivers, lakes, and oceans.

Red.location: Vermilion (Old), Fuchsia (Good), Route 12 (Super)
Red.instructions:
• Old Rod: Fishing Guru's house in Vermilion City (catches Magikarp).
• Good Rod: Fishing Guru's brother in Fuchsia City (catches Poliwag, Goldeen).
• Super Rod: Fishing Guru's brother on Route 12 south of Lavender Town (catches high-level Gyarados, Dratini, Psyduck).
Red.prerequisites: Talk to Fishing Gurus in each town

Blue.location: Vermilion (Old), Fuchsia (Good), Route 12 (Super)
Blue.instructions: Old Rod in Vermilion City, Good Rod in Fuchsia City, Super Rod on Route 12.
Blue.prerequisites: Talk to Fishing Gurus

FireRed.instructions:
• Old Rod: Vermilion City house next to Pokémon Center.
• Good Rod: Fuchsia City house next to Warden's home.
• Super Rod: Route 12 Fishing Guru house.

Ruby.instructions:
• Old Rod: Fisherman standing by the gym on Dewford Island (catches Magikarp, Tentacool).
• Good Rod: Fisherman on the east beach of Route 118 across from Mauville (catches Carvanha, Barboach).
• Super Rod: Fisherman in the cliff house north of Space Center in Mossdeep City (catches Sharpedo, Wailmer, Relicanth).
Ruby.prerequisites: Talk to Fishermen in Dewford, Route 118, and Mossdeep

Sapphire.location: Dewford (Old), Route 118 (Good), Mossdeep (Super)
Sapphire.instructions: Old Rod on Dewford Island, Good Rod on Route 118, Super Rod in Mossdeep City.
Sapphire.prerequisites: Talk to Fishermen

Emerald.instructions:
• Old Rod: Fisherman outside Dewford Gym.
• Good Rod: Fisherman on Route 118 east shore.
• Super Rod: Fisherman in house at north end of Mossdeep City.

items.name: Evolution Stones (Fire, Water, Thunder, Leaf, Moon, Sun, Shiny, Dusk, Dawn)
items.description: Elemental stones that radiate mysterious energy, triggering immediate evolution in compatible species.

Red.location: Celadon Department Store 4F (Fire, Water, Thunder, Leaf) / Mt. Moon (Moon)
Red.instructions: Fire, Water, and Thunder Stones can be purchased indefinitely on 4F of Celadon Department Store for 2,100 Pokédollars. Moon Stones are limited: find two in Mt. Moon, one in Rocket Hideout, and one in Pokémon Mansion.
Red.prerequisites: Reach Celadon City Department Store

FireRed.instructions: Buy Fire, Water, Thunder, and Leaf Stones at Celadon Dept Store 4F (2,100 Pokédollars). Sun Stone is found on Ruin Valley (Six Island). Moon Stone in Mt. Moon & Rocket Hideout.

Ruby.instructions:
• Fire Stone: Fiery Path (requires Strength HM04).
• Water Stone: Abandoned Ship (Room 3, require Dive HM08).
• Thunder Stone: New Mauville generator room (Wattson quest).
• Leaf Stone: Route 119.
• Sun Stone: Mossdeep Space Center (talk to Sailor).
• Moon Stone: Meteor Falls.
• Shard Exchange: Trade Red, Blue, Yellow, Green Shards to the Diving Hunter on Route 124 for respective stones!
Ruby.prerequisites: Dive HM08 / Shard Exchange on Route 124

Sapphire.location: Route 124 (Shard Hunter) / New Mauville / Abandoned Ship
Sapphire.instructions: Trade colored shards to the Diving Hunter on Route 124, or find individually in Fiery Path, New Mauville, and Abandoned Ship.
Sapphire.prerequisites: Dive HM08

Emerald.location: Route 124 Shard Hunter / Abandoned Ship / Fiery Path
Emerald.instructions: Collect Red, Blue, Yellow, and Green Shards from underwater dive trenches and exchange them at the Diving Treasure Hunter's house on Route 124 for Fire, Water, Thunder, and Leaf Stones.

Diamond.instructions: Dig in the Sinnoh Underground using the Explorer Kit to excavate unlimited Fire, Water, Thunder, Leaf, and Moon Stones. Shiny Stone is on Iron Island, Dusk Stone in Galactic Veilstone HQ, Dawn Stone in Mt. Coronet (Route 207 entrance).
Diamond.prerequisites: Explorer Kit from Eterna Underground Man

Scarlet.location: Delibird Presents & Overworld Sparkles
Scarlet.instructions: Fire, Water, Thunder, and Leaf Stones can be purchased at any Delibird Presents shop (Mesagoza, Cascarrafa, Levincia) for 3,000 Pokédollars after earning 3 Gym Badges. Sun, Moon, Shiny, Dusk, and Dawn Stones are found as glowing overworld ground sparkles across Paldea or auctioned at Porto Marinada.
Scarlet.prerequisites: 3 Gym Badges (Delibird Presents) or Porto Marinada Auction

Violet.location: Delibird Presents & Overworld Sparkles
Violet.instructions: Buy Fire, Water, Thunder, and Leaf Stones at Delibird Presents (3,000 Pokédollars after 3 Badges). Other stones found at Porto Marinada Auction.

Red.location: Route 12 (South of Lavender Town) and Route 16 (West of Celadon City)
Red.solution:
1. Acquire the Silph Scope by defeating Giovanni in the Rocket Hideout beneath the Celadon Game Corner.
2. Scale Pokémon Tower in Lavender Town and defeat the Ghost of Marowak on 6F.
3. Rescue Mr. Fuji on 7F; he will take you to his house in Lavender Town and gift you the Poké Flute.
4. Stand in front of either sleeping Snorlax and use the Poké Flute to wake it up into a Lv. 30 battle (Catch or defeat to permanently clear the road).
Red.prerequisites: Silph Scope, Poké Flute from Mr. Fuji

Blue.location: Route 12 and Route 16
Blue.solution: Clear Team Rocket from Celadon Hideout for the Silph Scope, save Mr. Fuji at Pokémon Tower for the Poké Flute, then play the flute to wake Snorlax.
Blue.prerequisites: Silph Scope, Poké Flute from Mr. Fuji

Yellow.location: Route 12 and Route 16
Yellow.solution: Obtain Silph Scope in Celadon Hideout, rescue Mr. Fuji from Pokémon Tower for the Poké Flute, and play it to battle Snorlax.
Yellow.prerequisites: Silph Scope, Poké Flute from Mr. Fuji

FireRed.location: Route 12 (South of Lavender) and Route 16 (West of Celadon)
FireRed.solution:
1. Defeat Giovanni in Celadon Rocket Hideout for the Silph Scope.
2. Climb Pokémon Tower in Lavender Town, soothe Marowak, and rescue Mr. Fuji on the top floor.
3. Receive the Poké Flute at Mr. Fuji's volunteer house.
4. Use the Poké Flute next to Snorlax to battle it at Lv. 30.
FireRed.prerequisites: Silph Scope, Poké Flute from Mr. Fuji

LeafGreen.location: Route 12 and Route 16
LeafGreen.solution: Defeat Giovanni for the Silph Scope, rescue Mr. Fuji from Pokémon Tower for the Poké Flute, and play the flute to clear Snorlax.
LeafGreen.prerequisites: Silph Scope, Poké Flute from Mr. Fuji

Gold.location: Route 11 (Blocking Diglett's Cave outside Vermilion City)
Gold.solution:
1. Restore power to the Kanto Power Plant by retrieving the stolen Machine Part from Cerulean Gym.
2. Visit the Lavender Radio Tower; the grateful Director will give you the EXPN Card (Expansion Card) for your Pokégear.
3. Go to Route 11, open your Pokégear Radio, and tune to the Poké Flute channel (top of the dial at 20.0).
4. Interact with the sleeping Snorlax to wake it up at Lv. 50.
Gold.prerequisites: Machine Part returned to Power Plant, EXPN Card for Pokégear Radio

Silver.location: Route 11 (Blocking Diglett's Cave outside Vermilion City)
Silver.solution: Restore the Power Plant, receive the EXPN Card from Lavender Radio Tower, tune to the Poké Flute broadcast, and interact with Snorlax.
Silver.prerequisites: EXPN Card for Pokégear Radio

HeartGold.solution:
1. Recover the Machine Part from Cerulean Gym and return it to the Power Plant manager on Route 10.
2. Speak to the Lavender Radio Tower director to install the EXPN Card.
3. Stand next to Snorlax on Route 11, tune the Pokégear Radio circle to the top-center (Poké Flute melody), and press A on Snorlax to initiate a Lv. 50 battle.
HeartGold.prerequisites: Power Plant restored, EXPN Card tuned to Poké Flute

SoulSilver.location: Route 11 / Diglett's Cave
SoulSilver.solution: Restore the Power Plant, acquire the EXPN Card in Lavender Town, broadcast the Poké Flute station, and wake Snorlax.
SoulSilver.prerequisites: Power Plant restored, EXPN Card tuned to Poké Flute

Gold.location: Route 36 (Junction to Ecruteak City & National Park)
Gold.solution:
1. Challenge and defeat Gym Leader Whitney in Goldenrod City to earn the Plain Badge.
2. Go to the Goldenrod Flower Shop (directly east of the gym) and talk to the florist girl to obtain the SquirtBottle.
3. Head north through Route 35 and National Park, or east through Route 36.
4. Walk up to the squirming tree and spray it with the SquirtBottle to trigger battle with Lv. 20 Sudowoodo.
5. Capture or faint it to open the road north to Ecruteak City and west to Violet City.
Gold.prerequisites: Plain Badge from Whitney, SquirtBottle from Goldenrod Flower Shop

Silver.location: Route 36
Silver.solution: Earn the Plain Badge from Whitney, claim the SquirtBottle from the Goldenrod Flower Shop, and water the strange tree on Route 36.
Silver.prerequisites: Plain Badge, SquirtBottle

Crystal.location: Route 36
Crystal.solution: Defeat Whitney in Goldenrod Gym for the Plain Badge, receive the SquirtBottle from the Flower Shop girl, and spray the tree on Route 36.
Crystal.prerequisites: Plain Badge, SquirtBottle

HeartGold.solution:
1. Defeat Gym Leader Whitney in Goldenrod Gym to earn the Plain Badge.
2. Visit the Goldenrod Flower Shop and talk to Floria and her sister to receive the SquirtBottle.
3. Approach the moving tree on Route 36 and interact with it to spray water.
4. Defeat or capture Lv. 20 Sudowoodo. Talk to the man on the right afterwards to receive TM08 Rock Smash.

SoulSilver.location: Route 36 (Intersection)
SoulSilver.solution: Defeat Whitney for the Plain Badge, get SquirtBottle from Goldenrod Flower Shop, and water the tree on Route 36.
SoulSilver.prerequisites: Plain Badge from Whitney, SquirtBottle

Ruby.solution:
1. When you arrive in Fortree City, an invisible obstacle blocks the Gym entrance.
2. Head east out of Fortree onto Route 120 and walk across the northern bridge until you find Steven Stone looking into the water.
3. Talk to Steven; he will give you the Devon Scope and demonstrate it by unmasking an invisible Lv. 30 Kecleon.
4. Return to Fortree City Gym and use the Devon Scope in front of the entrance to scare away the invisible Kecleon, unblocking the Gym for your match with Winona.
Ruby.prerequisites: Talk to Steven on Route 120 Bridge

Sapphire.location: Route 120 & Fortree City Gym
Sapphire.solution: Find Steven Stone on the bridge on Route 120 east of Fortree City. He gives you the Devon Scope to reveal invisible Kecleon, allowing you to unblock Fortree Gym.
Sapphire.prerequisites: Talk to Steven on Route 120 Bridge

Emerald.solution: Walk east from Fortree City onto Route 120. Steven Stone is waiting on the bridge and presents you with the Devon Scope after revealing a Kecleon. Use it in Fortree to access Gym Leader Winona.
Emerald.prerequisites: Talk to Steven on Route 120 Bridge

routes_and_roadblocks.name: Team Aqua / Magma Grunt Blockade in Slateport

Ruby.solution:
1. Team Magma grunts block the Oceanic Museum entrance.
2. Walk south to Stern's Shipyard in the harbor and talk to Dock on the 1st floor (who is examining blueprint schematics).
3. Dock tells you Captain Stern is missing at the Oceanic Museum.
4. Walk back north: the museum entrance is now unblocked! Pay 50 Pokédollars to enter, go up to the 2nd floor, and speak to Captain Stern to deliver the Devon Goods. Defeat the two Team Magma grunts who ambush you.
Ruby.prerequisites: Talk to Dock at Stern's Shipyard first

Sapphire.location: Slateport City (Oceanic Museum & Shipyard)
Sapphire.solution: Speak to Dock in the shipyard building to update the quest flag, then enter the Oceanic Museum on the north side, pay the entrance fee, and deliver the Devon Goods to Captain Stern on 2F.
Sapphire.prerequisites: Talk to Dock at Stern's Shipyard first

Emerald.solution: Visit Stern's Shipyard and talk to Dock on 1F. Head to the Oceanic Museum, pay the 50 Pokédollars fee, go to 2F, and defeat Team Aqua grunts to deliver the Devon Goods to Captain Stern.
Emerald.prerequisites: Talk to Dock at Stern's Shipyard first

Diamond.solution:
1. A flock of Psyduck clutching their heads blocks the northern pass on Route 210.
2. Defeat Gym Leader Crasher Wake in Pastoria City for the Fen Badge.
3. Talk to the Team Galactic Grunt outside Pastoria Great Marsh and pursue him east through Route 213 to Lake Valor.
4. Defeat the Grunt in battle; Cynthia will arrive and hand you the SecretPotion.
5. Return to Route 210 and use the SecretPotion on the Psyduck flock to cure their headaches; they will disperse into the tall grass, unlocking the path to Celestic Town.
Diamond.prerequisites: Fen Badge from Crasher Wake, SecretPotion from Cynthia

Pearl.solution: Earn the Fen Badge in Pastoria City, chase the Galactic Grunt to Lake Valor, receive the SecretPotion from Cynthia, and cure the Psyduck on Route 210.
Pearl.prerequisites: Fen Badge, SecretPotion from Cynthia

Platinum.solution: Defeat Crasher Wake, pursue the Galactic Grunt past Valor Lakefront, receive SecretPotion from Cynthia, and clear the Psyduck on Route 210.
Platinum.prerequisites: Fen Badge, SecretPotion from Cynthia

Red.instructions: Move Relearning does not exist in Pokémon Red, Blue, or Yellow. Any forgotten moves are lost permanently unless taught via TM or HM.

FireRed.cost: 2 Tiny Mushrooms or 1 Big Mushroom (harvested from wild Paras or Parasect in Mt. Moon / Safari Zone)
FireRed.instructions: Talk to the Move Maniac on Two Island. Pay with mushrooms to re-teach any level-up move your Pokémon previously learned.

LeafGreen.instructions: Talk to the Move Maniac on Two Island to relearn level-up moves in exchange for mushrooms.

Gold.instructions: In standalone Gold/Silver, Move Relearning is only accessible by connecting the cartridge to Pokémon Stadium 2 on Nintendo 64 after clearing Gym Leader Castle.

HeartGold.building: House south of Blackthorn Poké Mart
HeartGold.cost: 1 Heart Scale (Find with Rock Smash in Cianwood/Vermilion, or Pokéathlon Dome for 1,000 Pts)
HeartGold.instructions: Talk to the fat man in the house south of Blackthorn Poké Mart. Give him 1 Heart Scale to re-learn any move from your Pokémon's level-up moveset.

SoulSilver.building: House south of Blackthorn Poké Mart
SoulSilver.instructions: The Move Reminder in Blackthorn City re-teaches any move for 1 Heart Scale.

Ruby.building: House west of Poké Mart (Hearthome crater edge)
Ruby.cost: 1 Heart Scale (Found underwater with Itemfinder, or on wild Luvdisc with Thief/Covet on Route 128)
Ruby.instructions: Speak to the Move Tutor inside his house in Fallarbor Town. For 1 Heart Scale, he will teach your Pokémon any move it knew at a previous level.

Sapphire.instructions: Give 1 Heart Scale to the Move Tutor in Fallarbor Town to re-learn forgotten moves.

Emerald.instructions: The Move Tutor in Fallarbor Town re-teaches level-up moves in exchange for 1 Heart Scale. Tip: Fish with Super Rod on Route 128 for wild Luvdisc and use Thief to farm Heart Scales quickly!

Diamond.building: House near the lake southeast of Great Marsh
Diamond.cost: 1 Heart Scale (Found with Dowsing Machine or digging in the Sinnoh Underground)
Diamond.instructions: Give 1 Heart Scale to the Move Tutor in Pastoria City to re-learn any previous level-up move.

Pearl.building: House near the water in Pastoria City
Pearl.instructions: The Pastoria Move Tutor accepts 1 Heart Scale to remind your Pokémon of a move.

Platinum.building: House near the lake in Pastoria City
Platinum.instructions: The Move Tutor in Pastoria City re-teaches moves for 1 Heart Scale.

Scarlet.location: Party Menu (Anywhere in Overworld)
Scarlet.instructions: In Pokémon Scarlet, you can relearn any previously learned move for free at any time! Open the main menu (X), select the Pokémon, choose 'Check summary', navigate to the moves tab, and press (A) on 'Change moves' $ightarrow$ 'Remember moves'.

Violet.location: Party Menu (Anywhere in Overworld)
Violet.instructions: In Pokémon Violet, open your Pokémon's summary screen, go to the moves page, and press (A) to select 'Remember moves' for free instantly.

FireRed.building: House next to the Pokémon Center
FireRed.instructions: The Move Deleter is the only way in Gen 3 to erase HM moves (Cut, Fly, Surf, Strength, Flash, Rock Smash). He lives in the house directly beside Fuchsia Pokémon Center.

LeafGreen.instructions: Erases any move including HMs for free.

Ruby.building: House east of the Lilycove Department Store
Ruby.instructions: Visit the Move Deleter in Lilycove City to erase unwanted moves, including all HM moves.

Sapphire.instructions: Erases HM and normal moves for free.

Emerald.building: House north of Poké Mart / east of Department Store
Emerald.instructions: The Move Deleter in Lilycove City removes any move from your Pokémon, including Surf, Waterfall, and Dive.

HeartGold.building: House south of Blackthorn Poké Mart
HeartGold.instructions: The Move Deleter stands in the same house as the Move Reminder in Blackthorn City.

SoulSilver.building: House south of Blackthorn Poké Mart
SoulSilver.instructions: Erases HM moves for free in Blackthorn City.

Diamond.building: House north of Canalave Poké Mart
Diamond.instructions: The Move Deleter in Canalave City erases any move for free.

Pearl.instructions: Erases HM moves for free in Canalave City.

Platinum.instructions: Erases any move for free in Canalave City.

Red.building: House south of Lavender Pokémon Center
Red.instructions: The Name Rater assesses and changes the nicknames of Pokémon caught by your Trainer ID.

FireRed.building: House south of Lavender Pokémon Center
FireRed.instructions: Changes nicknames for your own Pokémon.

Gold.building: House near the magnetic train station / Radio Tower
Gold.instructions: The Name Rater lives in the house directly north of Goldenrod Gym.

HeartGold.instructions: Changes your Pokémon's nicknames for free.

Ruby.building: House north of the Contest Hall / Battle Tent
Ruby.instructions: The Name Rater lives in the brown house in northern Slateport City.

Sapphire.instructions: Changes nicknames in Slateport City.

Emerald.instructions: The Name Rater in Slateport City renames any Pokémon carrying your Trainer ID for free.

Diamond.instructions: The Name Rater sits on 1F of the tall condominium building in Eterna City.

Scarlet.location: Party Summary (Anywhere in Overworld)
Scarlet.instructions: In Pokémon Scarlet, change any Pokémon's nickname at any time for free! Open your Pokémon's summary screen and press (X) to rename.

Violet.location: Party Summary (Anywhere in Overworld)
Violet.instructions: Open the Pokémon summary screen and press (X) to rename anytime for free.

Red.instructions: Raises one Pokémon at a time (no breeding in Gen 1). Gained experience equals steps taken.

FireRed.building: Four Island Pokémon Day Care (Sevii Islands)
FireRed.instructions: The Route 5 Day Care only raises one Pokémon. To breed Pokémon for Eggs, use the Pokémon Day Care on Four Island!

Gold.building: Day Care cottage with outdoor yard
Gold.instructions: Accepts two Pokémon. If compatible, the Day Care Man in the yard will discover a Pokémon Egg! Talk to him to claim the Egg and hatch by walking.

HeartGold.instructions: Leave a male and female or Ditto to produce Eggs. The Day Care Man will call your Pokégear when an Egg is ready if you register him!

Ruby.instructions: Leave two compatible Pokémon to produce Eggs. The long horizontal road from Verdanturf through Mauville to Route 118 is the optimal cycling path to hatch Eggs quickly!

Sapphire.instructions: Breed Pokémon on Route 117 between Mauville City and Verdanturf Town.

Emerald.instructions: Route 117 Day Care. Tip: Keep a Pokémon with Magma Armor or Flame Body (like Slugma or Camerupt) in your party to cut the steps needed to hatch Eggs in half!

Diamond.instructions: Located in Solaceon Town. The vertical road extending through Solaceon and Route 209/210 is ideal for hatching Eggs on the Bicycle.

Scarlet.location: Picnic Feature (Anywhere in Overworld)
Scarlet.instructions: In Pokémon Scarlet, breeding occurs during Picnics! Set up a picnic table outside towns with compatible Pokémon or Ditto in your party. Eat an Egg Power sandwich (e.g. Great Peanut Butter Sandwich) and check the basket at the foot of the picnic table to collect multiple Eggs rapidly.

Violet.location: Picnic Feature (Anywhere in Overworld)
Violet.instructions: Breeding occurs during Picnics. Make an Egg Power sandwich, wait a few minutes, and collect Eggs from the basket.

Ruby.strategy: Mudkip (Water Gun) or Treecko (Absorb) sweep easily. If you chose Torchic, evolve it into Combusken at Level 16 for Double Kick (Fighting 2x super effective), or catch a wild Wingull (Water Gun) on Route 104, Shroomish (Absorb) in Petalburg Woods, or Lotad/Seedot.

Sapphire.strategy: Use Water- or Grass-type moves. Watch out for Nosepass using Rock Tomb to slow your speed and Harden to buff its already massive 135 base Defense.

Emerald.strategy: In Emerald, Roxanne has two Geodudes. Mudkip with Water Gun or Treecko with Absorb OHKO the Geodudes (4x quad weak). If you chose Torchic, evolve into Combusken at Lv. 16 for Double Kick, or use Wingull (Route 104) / Shroomish (Petalburg Woods).

Ruby.strategy: Swampert / Marshtomp or any Water/Ground-type dominates with Mud Shot, Water Pulse, or Surf. Beware of Torkoal's devastating Overheat (140 BP) on Turn 1!

Emerald.strategy: In Emerald, Flannery's Torkoal holds a White Herb that instantly negates the harsh Sp. Atk drop from Overheat! Marshtomp or Swampert with Surf or Mud Shot deals 4x quad damage to Numel and Camerupt (Fire/Ground) and 2x damage to Torkoal. Alternatively, bring Gyarados or Azumarill.

Ruby.strategy: Ground-types completely trivialize Wattson! Marshtomp or Geodude (Granite Cave) take zero Electric damage and hit Magnemite and Magneton for 4x quad super-effective damage with Mud Shot or Magnitude. Watch out for Voltorb using Self-Destruct.

Sapphire.strategy: Use Ground-types like Marshtomp, Geodude, or Shedinja (which is completely immune to all of Wattson's attacks via Wonder Guard!).

Emerald.strategy: In Emerald, Wattson adds Manectric (Lv. 24) with Bite and Quick Attack! Marshtomp (Water/Ground) is completely immune to Electric moves and decimates Magneton with Mud Shot (4x quad weak). If you do not have Marshtomp, catch a Geodude or Aron in Granite Cave.

Red.strategy: Bulbasaur (Vine Whip) or Squirtle (Bubble) deal 4x quad super-effective damage and OHKO Geodude and Onix. If you chose Charmander, catch a Mankey (Low Kick/Karate Chop on Route 22), Nidoran (Double Kick at Lv. 12), or Butterfree (Confusion at Lv. 12). Beware of Onix using Bide!

Yellow.strategy: Pikachu's Electric attacks do ZERO damage to Rock/Ground types! Catch a Mankey on Route 22 west of Viridian City (learns Low Kick at Lv. 9), or catch Nidoran male/female and level to 12 for Double Kick.

FireRed.strategy: Bulbasaur (Vine Whip) and Squirtle (Water Gun) destroy Brock easily. Charmander learns Metal Claw at Level 13 (Steel 2x super effective against Rock)! Alternatively, catch Mankey on Route 22 for Low Kick.
Misty's Starmie is fast and hits hard with Water Pulse (which can confuse). Use Electric or Grass Pokémon like Pikachu or Bellsprout. Avoid Rock, Ground, or Fire types.

Red.strategy: Starmie has high Special and uses Bubblebeam. Grass or Electric moves can overpower it quickly.

FireRed.strategy: Lt. Surge's Raichu uses Thunderbolt, Shock Wave, and Double Team. A Dugtrio caught from Diglett's Cave is immune to Electric and sweeps with Dig.

Red.strategy: Raichu has high speed and hits hard. Ground types like Dugtrio or Geodude make this battle effortless.

recommendedCounters: Machop (in-game trade 'Muscle' in Goldenrod Dept Store for Drowzee)

Gold.strategy: Whitney's Miltank is notorious for Rollout and Attract. Trade a female Drowzee for Machop in Goldenrod Department Store 5F to sweep with Low Kick, or use Geodude with Defense Curl to resist Rollout.

Silver.strategy: Miltank builds unstoppable momentum with Rollout. Female Machop from Goldenrod Dept Store trade resists Attract and hits for 2x super-effective Fighting damage.

Crystal.strategy: Use female Machop from Goldenrod trade or Geodude/Onix with Rock/Ground resistance.

HeartGold.strategy: Miltank has Scrappy (hitting Ghosts) and uses Milk Drink. Use Machop from Goldenrod Dept Store.

SoulSilver.strategy: Trade for female Machop 'Muscle' in Goldenrod Dept Store.

Red.strategy: Erika uses Grass/Poison types. Fire, Flying, Ice, and Psychic attacks melt her team.

FireRed.strategy: Erika's team relies on status moves like Sleep Powder and Stun Spore. Equip Chesto Berries or use Fire-types.

Gold.strategy: Catch a Geodude in Dark Cave or Route 46; Rock Throw resists Flying moves and destroys Pidgey and Pidgeotto.

Silver.strategy: Geodude from Route 46 trivializes Falkner with 4x Rock resistance.

Ruby.strategy: Electric and Grass moves sweep. Milotic uses Recover and Ice Beam.

Sapphire.strategy: Electric-types counter most; use Grass against Whiscash (Water/Ground 4x weak).

Emerald.strategy: In Emerald, Juan is the gym leader while Wallace is the Champion! Kingdra uses Double Team and Rest with Chesto Berry.

moveset.source: TM13 (Mauville Game Corner or Abandoned Ship)

inGameBuild.heldItem: Leftovers (passive healing) or Mystic Water / Soft Sand (+20% STAB)
inGameBuild.tacticalAdvice: Swampert only possesses one single defensive weakness in the entire game: Grass (4x quad weak). Immunity to Electric-type moves completely shuts down Wattson (Mauville Gym) and rival Raichu/Manectric. Always teach Ice Beam to counter Grass-type and Dragon-type foes like Drake's Salamence!

Charizard has a 4x quad weakness to Rock-type attacks (Rock Slide/Stone Edge). In Gen 1 / FireRed, teach Earthquake or Brick Break to counter Rock- and Electric-types. Flamethrower melts Erika (Grass), Koga (Poison/Bug), and Lorelei (Ice) with ease!

inGameBuild.heldItem: Black Sludge (heals Poison-types) or Spell Tag
inGameBuild.tacticalAdvice: With blazing base 110 Speed and 130 Special Attack, Gengar is one of the deadliest sweepers in Kanto, Johto, and Sinnoh. Immunity to Normal, Fighting, and Ground (via Levitate in Gens 3-6) lets Gengar switch in for free against common moves.

inGameBuild.heldItem: Miracle Seed (+20% Grass damage) or Leftovers
inGameBuild.tacticalAdvice: With base 120 Speed, Sceptile outspeeds nearly every in-game opponent. Leaf Blade has a high critical-hit ratio and shreds Roxanne, Wallace, Juan, and Glacia's Water-types!

Blaziken's Fire/Fighting typing gives it unmatched offensive coverage in Hoenn. Bulk Up buffs Attack and Defense simultaneously, allowing Blaziken to sweep Norman's Slaking, Sidney's Dark-types, and Glacia's Ice-types.

moveset.source: Wayward Cave Secret Room TM26 or Level up

inGameBuild.heldItem: Yache Berry (cuts 4x Ice damage in half) or Soft Sand
inGameBuild.tacticalAdvice: Garchomp has unmatched 102 base Speed and 130 base Attack. Beware of its 4x quad weakness to Ice-type moves; holding a Yache Berry allows it to survive an Ice Beam and OHKO in return.

potion.description: Essential early-to-mid adventure restorative sprays that heal 20 HP (Potion) or 50-60 HP (Super Potion).
