azure_flute.name: Azure Flute (Hall of Origin / Arceus)
azure_flute.description: A heavenly flute that echoes with an otherworldly sound, summoning glowing glass stairs at Spear Pillar into the Hall of Origin.
azure_flute.generalInstructions: Stand on the first step tile at Spear Pillar. Blow the Azure Flute; glowing crystal steps materialize ascending to Level 80 Arceus!

Diamond.instructions: Climb Mt. Coronet to the Spear Pillar summit with the Azure Flute. Stand on the entrance tile and play the flute to summon glowing crystalline stairs ascending to the Hall of Origin, where the Original One Arceus awaits (Lv. 80).
Diamond.prerequisites: Azure Flute received via event distribution and National Pokédex obtained

Platinum.instructions: Climb Mt. Coronet to the Spear Pillar summit with the Azure Flute. Stand on the entrance tile and play the flute to summon glowing crystalline stairs ascending to the Hall of Origin, where the Original One Arceus awaits (Lv. 80).
Platinum.prerequisites: Azure Flute received via event distribution and National Pokédex obtained

Pearl.instructions: Climb Mt. Coronet to the Spear Pillar summit with the Azure Flute. Stand on the entrance tile and play the flute to summon glowing crystalline stairs ascending to the Hall of Origin, where the Original One Arceus awaits (Lv. 80).
Pearl.prerequisites: Azure Flute received via event distribution and National Pokédex obtained

evolution_stones.name: Evolution Stones (Fire, Water, Thunder, Leaf, Moon)
evolution_stones.description: Elemental stones that radiate mysterious energy, triggering immediate evolution in specific Pokémon species (e.g. Eevee, Pikachu, Growlithe, Staryu, Exeggcute, Clefairy).
evolution_stones.generalLocation: Celadon Department Store 4F (Kanto) / Route 124 Diving Treasure Hunter (Hoenn)
evolution_stones.generalInstructions: Celadon Dept Store 4F sells Fire, Water, Thunder, and Leaf Stones for 2,100 Pokédollars. In Hoenn, exchange Blue/Red/Yellow/Green Shards with the Treasure Hunter on Route 124.
evolution_stones.generalPrerequisites: Visit Department Store or collect colored Shards

Red.location: Celadon Dept Store 4F
Red.instructions: Buy Fire, Water, Thunder, Leaf Stones for 2,100 Pokédollars on 4F. Find Moon Stones in Mt. Moon and Rocket Hideout.
Red.prerequisites: Reach Celadon City

Ruby.instructions: Exchange colored shards found while diving on Route 124 with the Treasure Hunter for Water, Fire, Thunder, and Leaf stones.
Ruby.prerequisites: HM08 Dive

metal_coat.name: Metal Coat (Scizor & Steelix)
metal_coat.description: A special metallic film that boosts Steel-type moves by 20% and triggers trade evolution for Scyther -> Scizor and Onix -> Steelix.
metal_coat.generalLocation: S.S. Aqua Grandfather / Wild Magnemite holds (5%)
metal_coat.generalInstructions: Find a little girl running around on the S.S. Aqua ferry and return her to her grandfather; he rewards you with the Metal Coat.
metal_coat.generalPrerequisites: Complete Johto League for S.S. Ticket

Gold.location: S.S. Aqua (Fast Ship)
Gold.instructions: Reunite lost granddaughter with her grandfather on S.S. Aqua to receive Metal Coat.
Gold.prerequisites: S.S. Ticket from Professor Elm

kings_rock.name: King's Rock (Slowking & Politoed)
kings_rock.description: A crown-shaped rock that grants a 10% flinch chance to attacks and evolves Poliwhirl -> Politoed and Slowpoke -> Slowking when traded.
kings_rock.generalInstructions: Surf into the hidden back chamber of Slowpoke Well (B2F) with Strength to find a man who awards you the King's Rock.

Gold.location: Slowpoke Well B2F
Gold.instructions: Surf to the bottom floor of Slowpoke Well in Azalea Town to receive King's Rock.
Gold.prerequisites: HM03 Surf & Strength

choice_items.name: Choice Band, Choice Specs & Choice Scarf
choice_items.description: High-risk, high-reward battle items that boost Attack, Sp. Atk, or Speed by 50%, but lock the Pokémon into using only one move until switched out.
choice_items.generalLocation: Battle Frontier / Battle Tower (48 BP) & Mesagoza Delibird Presents
choice_items.generalInstructions: Earn Battle Points in post-game battle facilities or purchase for 100,000 Pokédollars at Delibird Presents in Cascarrafa/Mesagoza.
choice_items.generalPrerequisites: Post-Game Battle Facility or 4 Gym Badges in SV

Emerald.instructions: Exchange 48 BP for Choice Band at the Service Corner.

focus_sash.name: Focus Sash & Focus Band
focus_sash.description: An essential competitive sash that guarantees the holder will survive any single fatal hit with 1 HP remaining when at 100% full health.
focus_sash.generalInstructions: Show the level-requested Pokémon to the old man on Route 221, or buy at Delibird Presents for 50,000 Pokédollars.

Diamond.instructions: Old man on Route 221 gifts Focus Sash after showing a Pokémon of the requested level.
Diamond.prerequisites: Surf to Route 221

snorlax.name: Snorlax (Sleeping Giant Roadblocks)
snorlax.description: Massive sleeping Pokémon blocking crucial highway intersections across Kanto (Route 12 and Route 16) and Vermilion City entrance in Johto.
snorlax.generalLocation: Route 12 (South of Lavender) & Route 16 (West of Celadon)
snorlax.generalInstructions: Obtain the Poké Flute from Mr. Fuji in Lavender Town. Play the flute next to Snorlax to awaken Level 30 wild Snorlax (holding Leftovers!).

Red.location: Route 12 & Route 16
Red.instructions: Play Poké Flute to wake and battle Level 30 Snorlax.
Red.prerequisites: Poké Flute

FireRed.instructions: Play Poké Flute to wake Level 30 Snorlax.

Gold.location: Route 11 (Blocking Diglett's Cave outside Vermilion City)
Gold.instructions:
1. Restore power to the Kanto Power Plant by retrieving the stolen Machine Part from Cerulean Gym.
2. Visit the Lavender Radio Tower to receive the EXPN Card (Expansion Card) for your Pokégear.
3. Stand next to Snorlax on Route 11, open Pokégear Radio, and tune to the Poké Flute channel (top of the dial at 20.0).
4. Interact with Snorlax to wake it up into a Lv. 50 battle.
Gold.prerequisites: Machine Part returned to Power Plant, EXPN Card for Pokégear Radio

Silver.location: Route 11 (Blocking Diglett's Cave outside Vermilion City)
Silver.instructions:
1. Restore power to the Kanto Power Plant by retrieving the stolen Machine Part from Cerulean Gym.
2. Visit the Lavender Radio Tower to receive the EXPN Card (Expansion Card) for your Pokégear.
3. Stand next to Snorlax on Route 11, open Pokégear Radio, and tune to the Poké Flute channel (top of the dial at 20.0).
4. Interact with Snorlax to wake it up into a Lv. 50 battle.
Silver.prerequisites: Machine Part returned to Power Plant, EXPN Card for Pokégear Radio

Crystal.location: Route 11 (Blocking Diglett's Cave outside Vermilion City)
Crystal.instructions:
1. Restore power to the Kanto Power Plant by retrieving the stolen Machine Part from Cerulean Gym.
2. Visit the Lavender Radio Tower to receive the EXPN Card (Expansion Card) for your Pokégear.
3. Stand next to Snorlax on Route 11, open Pokégear Radio, and tune to the Poké Flute channel (top of the dial at 20.0).
4. Interact with Snorlax to wake it up into a Lv. 50 battle.
Crystal.prerequisites: Machine Part returned to Power Plant, EXPN Card for Pokégear Radio

HeartGold.instructions:
1. Recover the Machine Part from Cerulean Gym and return it to the Power Plant manager on Route 10.
2. Speak to the Lavender Radio Tower director to install the EXPN Card.
3. Stand next to Snorlax on Route 11, tune the Pokégear Radio circle to the top-center (Poké Flute melody), and press A on Snorlax to initiate a Lv. 50 battle.
HeartGold.prerequisites: Power Plant restored, EXPN Card tuned to Poké Flute

SoulSilver.location: Route 11 / Diglett's Cave (Vermilion City)
SoulSilver.instructions:
1. Recover the Machine Part from Cerulean Gym and return it to the Power Plant manager on Route 10.
2. Speak to the Lavender Radio Tower director to install the EXPN Card.
3. Stand next to Snorlax on Route 11, tune the Pokégear Radio circle to the top-center (Poké Flute melody), and press A on Snorlax to initiate a Lv. 50 battle.
SoulSilver.prerequisites: Power Plant restored, EXPN Card tuned to Poké Flute

sudowoodo.name: Sudowoodo (Route 36 Weird Tree)
sudowoodo.description: A peculiar rocking tree blocking the Route 36 junction between Violet, Goldenrod, and Ecruteak City.
sudowoodo.generalInstructions: Obtain the SquirtBottle from the Goldenrod Flower Shop after earning the Plain Badge. Spray the tree; it attacks as a Level 20 Rock-type Sudowoodo!

Gold.location: Route 36
Gold.instructions: Spray Sudowoodo with SquirtBottle to battle Level 20 Sudowoodo.
Gold.prerequisites: Plain Badge from Whitney, SquirtBottle from Goldenrod Flower Shop

HeartGold.instructions: Use SquirtBottle on the strange tree to open the path to Ecruteak City.
HeartGold.prerequisites: Plain Badge from Whitney, SquirtBottle from Goldenrod Flower Shop

master_ball.name: Master Ball (100% Guaranteed Catch & Per-Game Best Targets)
aliases: who to use master ball on
master_ball.description: The pinnacle of Poké Ball engineering (255x / 100% guaranteed capture rate). Includes exact acquisition locations and the #1 recommended target Pokémon for every mainline game from Gen 1 to Gen 9.
master_ball.generalLocation: Silph Co. 11F (Kanto), Prof. Elm (Johto), Lilycove Hideout (Hoenn), Veilstone Galactic HQ (Sinnoh), Prof. Juniper (Unova), Laverre Factory (Kalos), Aether Paradise (Alola), Postwick (Galar), Academy (Paldea)
master_ball.generalInstructions: Always save your Master Ball for Turn-1 fleeing roamers (Raikou, Entei, Latias, Latios, Mesprit, Cresselia, Tornadus, Thundurus — especially in FireRed/LeafGreen where Roar permanently deletes Raikou/Entei!), high-level self-healing bosses (Lv. 70 Mewtwo, Lv. 80 ORAS Space Deoxys, Lv. 80 Calyrex), or Shiny Pokémon about to faint/self-destruct.
master_ball.generalPrerequisites: Defeat the Villainous Team Boss or Become Regional Champion

Red.location: Silph Co. 11F Boardroom (Saffron City) — Target: Mewtwo (Cerulean Cave B1F)
Red.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Obtain the Card Key on Silph Co. 5F, take the 3F warp pad to 7F (beat Rival Blue & claim Lapras), then warp to 11F and defeat Giovanni. Speak to the Silph Co. President for the Master Ball.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — MEWTWO (Lv. 70, Cerulean Cave B1F): Catch rate 3, knows Recover, Psychic, Amnesia, and Swift. Because Gen 1 Ultra Balls can completely miss high-HP legendaries unless asleep/frozen, Mewtwo is the undisputed #1 use of your Master Ball!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Articuno (Seafoam Islands), Zapdos (Power Plant), or Moltres (Victory Road) — though all 3 birds stay stationary and lack Recover, so catch them with Ultra Balls + Sleep Powder.
Red.prerequisites: Clear Silph Co. 11F Team Rocket Invasion

Blue.location: Silph Co. 11F Boardroom (Saffron City) — Target: Mewtwo (Cerulean Cave B1F)
Blue.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Giovanni on 11F of Silph Co. in Saffron City and speak to the President.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — MEWTWO (Lv. 70, Cerulean Cave B1F): Base catch rate 3 with infinite PP Recover and +2 Special Amnesia boosts. Use the Master Ball immediately on Turn 1!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Zapdos (Power Plant) or Articuno (Seafoam Islands).
Blue.prerequisites: Clear Silph Co. 11F Team Rocket Invasion

Yellow.location: Silph Co. 11F Boardroom (Saffron City) — Target: Mewtwo (Cerulean Cave B1F)
Yellow.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Jessie & James and Giovanni on Silph Co. 11F in Saffron City, then talk to the Silph President.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — MEWTWO (Lv. 70, Cerulean Cave B1F): The strongest Pokémon in Gen 1 (catch rate 3, spams Recover). Save your Master Ball exclusively for Mewtwo!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Zapdos (Power Plant) or Moltres (Victory Road).
Yellow.prerequisites: Defeat Giovanni at Silph Co. 11F

Gold.location: Prof. Elm's Lab (New Bark Town) — Target: Roaming Raikou or Entei
Gold.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Clair in Blackthorn Gym (and pass the Dragon's Den Shrine quiz) to earn the Rising Badge, then return to New Bark Town and talk to Professor Elm. (Bonus: Match all 5 digits at Goldenrod Radio Tower Lucky Number Show).
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — RAIKOU OR ENTEI (Lv. 40 Johto Roamers): After awakening at Burned Tower, Raikou and Entei roam Johto's routes and flee on Turn 1—even while asleep or frozen unless trapped by Mean Look/Spider Web—and both carry Roar to force-end battles!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Lugia (Lv. 70 in Gold at Whirl Islands) or Ho-Oh (Lv. 40 at Tin Tower) — both are stationary so you can save right in front of them and use Ultra Balls.
Gold.prerequisites: All 8 Johto Gym Badges (Rising Badge)

Silver.location: Prof. Elm's Lab (New Bark Town) — Target: Roaming Raikou or Entei
Silver.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Earn the 8th Johto Badge (Rising Badge) from Clair and speak to Professor Elm in New Bark Town.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — RAIKOU OR ENTEI (Lv. 40 Johto Roamers): Both roamers flee immediately on Turn 1 and know Roar. Using the Master Ball on Raikou or Entei saves hours of Haunter/Jynx Mean Look + Sleep setups!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Ho-Oh (Lv. 70 in Silver at Tin Tower) or Lugia (Lv. 40 at Whirl Islands).
Silver.prerequisites: All 8 Johto Gym Badges (Rising Badge)

Crystal.location: Prof. Elm's Lab (New Bark Town) — Target: Roaming Raikou or Entei
Crystal.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Earn all 8 Johto Badges and talk to Professor Elm in New Bark Town.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — RAIKOU OR ENTEI (Lv. 40 Johto Roamers): In Crystal, you MUST capture all three Legendary Beasts (Suicune at Tin Tower, plus roaming Raikou and Entei) to receive the Rainbow Wing and unlock Lv. 60 Ho-Oh! Since Suicune is stationary in Crystal, use your Master Ball on Raikou or Entei.
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Lugia (Lv. 60, Whirl Islands) or Celebi (Lv. 30, Ilex Forest Shrine).
Crystal.prerequisites: All 8 Johto Gym Badges (Rising Badge)

Ruby.location: Team Magma Hideout (Lilycove City) — Target: Roaming Latios
Ruby.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Infiltrate the Team Magma Hideout in the cove northeast of Lilycove City after visiting Mt. Pyre. In the Magma Leader's office, pick up the top-left of the 4 item balls (the other two are Nuggets and two are Lv. 30 Electrodes). ⚠️ WARNING: If you defeat Admin Courtney and exit the hideout without picking it up, the entrance seals permanently! (Bonus: Lilycove Dept. Store Lottery 5-digit match).
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — LATIOS (Lv. 40 Hoenn Roamer): Unlocks after beating the Elite Four; flees on Turn 1 across Hoenn routes.
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Rayquaza (Lv. 70, Sky Pillar — knows Outrage + Rest) or Groudon (Lv. 45, Cave of Origin).
Ruby.prerequisites: Clear Mt. Pyre Summit & Enter Lilycove Magma Hideout

Sapphire.location: Team Aqua Hideout (Lilycove City) — Target: Roaming Latias
Sapphire.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Enter the Team Aqua Hideout northeast of Lilycove City. Inside Captain Archie's quarters, solve the warp pad puzzle and grab the Master Ball among the 4 Poké Balls (two are Electrodes). ⚠️ WARNING: Permanently missable if you beat Admin Matt and leave the hideout!
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — LATIAS (Lv. 40 Hoenn Roamer): Roams Hoenn post-game and flees immediately on Turn 1.
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Rayquaza (Lv. 70, Sky Pillar) or Kyogre (Lv. 45, Cave of Origin).
Sapphire.prerequisites: Clear Mt. Pyre Summit & Enter Lilycove Aqua Hideout

Emerald.location: Team Aqua Hideout (Lilycove City) — Target: Roaming Latias/Latios or Rayquaza
Emerald.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: After clearing Team Magma's Jagged Pass base, infiltrate the Team Aqua Hideout in Lilycove City. Take the warp pads to Archie's room where 4 item balls sit on a platform (2 Electrodes, 1 Nugget, 1 Master Ball).
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — LATIAS OR LATIOS (Lv. 40 Post-Game Roamer): After beating Champion Wallace, Mom asks whether the TV news report mentioned a RED (Latias) or BLUE (Latios) Pokémon. Because it roams Hoenn and flees on Turn 1, the Master Ball guarantees instant capture!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Rayquaza (Lv. 70 at Sky Pillar BEFORE the 8th Gym — catching Rayquaza at Lv. 70 with the Master Ball lets you sweep Juan and the entire Elite Four effortlessly!).
Emerald.prerequisites: Clear Magma Hideout in Jagged Pass & Enter Lilycove Aqua Hideout

FireRed.location: Silph Co. 11F (Saffron City) — Target: Roaming Raikou/Entei (Roar Bug!) or Mewtwo
FireRed.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Giovanni on Silph Co. 11F in Saffron City and speak to the President.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — ROAMING RAIKOU, ENTEI, OR SUICUNE (Lv. 50 Post-Game Kanto Roamer): Which beast roams depends on your starter (Bulbasaur -> Entei, Charmander -> Suicune, Squirtle -> Raikou). ⚠️ CRITICAL GEN 3 GLITCH: In FireRed/LeafGreen, if wild Raikou or Entei uses ROAR while trapped by Mean Look/Shadow Tag, a programming bug permanently deletes the roamer from your save file forever! Always use the Master Ball on the Roaming Beast!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Mewtwo (Lv. 70, Cerulean Cave B1F — catch rate 3 with Recover and Safeguard).

LeafGreen.location: Silph Co. 11F (Saffron City) — Target: Roaming Raikou/Entei (Roar Bug!) or Mewtwo
LeafGreen.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Giovanni on Silph Co. 11F in Saffron City and talk to the Silph President.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — ROAMING RAIKOU, ENTEI, OR SUICUNE (Lv. 50 Post-Game Roamer): ⚠️ CRITICAL BUG WARNING: If roaming Raikou or Entei uses Roar in battle, it vanishes permanently from your save file due to a Gen 3 Roar glitch! Never risk fighting Raikou or Entei without the Master Ball.
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Mewtwo (Lv. 70, Cerulean Cave B1F).
LeafGreen.prerequisites: Defeat Giovanni at Silph Co. 11F

Diamond.location: Team Galactic HQ (Veilstone City) — Target: Roaming Mesprit or Cresselia
Diamond.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: After earning 7 Badges (Snowpoint Gym), infiltrate Team Galactic HQ in Veilstone City using the Storage Key and Galactic Key. Defeat Boss Cyrus on 4F; he hands you the Master Ball directly.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — MESPRIT (Lv. 50) OR CRESSELIA (Lv. 50): Both roam Sinnoh and flee on Turn 1! ⚠️ DO NOT waste your Master Ball on Dialga at Spear Pillar—Dialga's catch rate in Diamond is 30 (10x easier than normal legendaries, same as Chatot) and can be caught in 1–3 Dusk/Ultra Balls!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Giratina (Lv. 70 in Turnback Cave) or Heatran (Lv. 70 in Stark Mountain).
Diamond.prerequisites: 7 Gym Badges & Defeat Cyrus at Veilstone Galactic HQ

Pearl.location: Team Galactic HQ (Veilstone City) — Target: Roaming Mesprit or Cresselia
Pearl.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Boss Cyrus inside Team Galactic HQ in Veilstone City after the 7th Gym Badge.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — MESPRIT (Lv. 50) OR CRESSELIA (Lv. 50): Both roam Sinnoh and flee immediately. ⚠️ DO NOT use the Master Ball on Palkia at Spear Pillar—Palkia has an elevated catch rate of 30 and goes down easily to Dusk Balls or Net Balls (Water-type)!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Giratina (Lv. 70, Turnback Cave) or Heatran (Lv. 70, Stark Mountain).
Pearl.prerequisites: 7 Gym Badges & Defeat Cyrus at Veilstone Galactic HQ

Platinum.location: Team Galactic HQ (Veilstone City) — Target: Roaming Mesprit, Cresselia, or Kanto Birds
Platinum.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Cyrus inside Team Galactic's Veilstone HQ after earning the Icicle Badge.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — FIVE SINNOH ROAMERS (Mesprit Lv. 50, Cresselia Lv. 50, Articuno Lv. 60, Zapdos Lv. 60, Moltres Lv. 60): Platinum has FIVE separate roaming legendaries that flee on Turn 1! Use your Master Ball on Mesprit, Cresselia, or your favorite roaming Kanto Bird.
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Origin Forme Giratina (Lv. 47 in Distortion World) or Arceus (Lv. 80 at Hall of Origin).
Platinum.prerequisites: 7 Gym Badges & Defeat Cyrus at Veilstone Galactic HQ

HeartGold.location: Prof. Elm's Lab (New Bark Town) — Target: Roaming Raikou, Entei, or Latias
HeartGold.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Earn all 8 Johto Badges (beat Clair & complete Dragon's Den Shrine) and return to Professor Elm in New Bark Town.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — RAIKOU (Lv. 40), ENTEI (Lv. 40), OR LATIAS (Lv. 35 in Kanto): HeartGold has THREE roaming legendaries that flee on Turn 1 (Raikou and Entei in Johto; Latias in Kanto after restoring the Copycat's Lost Item).
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Mewtwo (Lv. 70, Cerulean Cave) or Ho-Oh / Lugia (Lv. 45/70).

SoulSilver.location: Prof. Elm's Lab (New Bark Town) — Target: Roaming Raikou, Entei, or Latios
SoulSilver.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Earn all 8 Johto Badges and speak to Professor Elm in New Bark Town.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — RAIKOU (Lv. 40), ENTEI (Lv. 40), OR LATIOS (Lv. 35 in Kanto): All three roam the region map and flee on Turn 1. Use your Master Ball on whichever roamer has the best Nature/IVs or to skip the Mean Look setup!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Mewtwo (Lv. 70, Cerulean Cave) or Ho-Oh (Lv. 70, Bell Tower).
SoulSilver.prerequisites: All 8 Johto Gym Badges

Black.location: Opelucid City (from Prof. Juniper) — Target: Roaming Tornadus or Kyurem
Black.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Drayden in Opelucid Gym to earn your 8th Unova Badge (Legend Badge). As you walk toward the Route 10 gate, Professor Juniper stops you and gifts you the Master Ball. (2nd Master Ball: Trade with 50+ distinct Trainer IDs and talk to the sunglasses man in Castelia Pokémon Center).
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — TORNADUS (Lv. 40 Unova Roamer): Roams Unova inside torrential rainstorms after visiting Route 7 and flees on Turn 1. ⚠️ DO NOT use the Master Ball on Reshiram at N's Castle—Reshiram has a high catch rate of 45 and the story forces you to catch it easily with Ultra/Quick Balls!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Kyurem (Lv. 75 in Giant Chasm, catch rate 3).
Black.prerequisites: Defeat Drayden for 8th Unova Badge

White.location: Opelucid City (from Prof. Juniper) — Target: Roaming Thundurus or Kyurem
White.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Iris in Opelucid Gym for the 8th Badge; Professor Juniper hands you the Master Ball outside the Route 10 gate.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — THUNDURUS (Lv. 40 Unova Roamer): Roams Unova in thunderstorms and flees immediately on Turn 1. ⚠️ Never use the Master Ball on Zekrom (catch rate 45).
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Kyurem (Lv. 75 in Giant Chasm, catch rate 3).
White.prerequisites: Defeat Iris for 8th Unova Badge

Black 2.location: Mistralton City (Prof. Juniper) + Plasma Frigate (Colress) — Target: Kyurem & Latios
Black 2.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET (2 MASTER BALLS!): First Master Ball is gifted by Professor Juniper inside Mistralton Pokémon Center before Skyla's Gym. Second Master Ball is won by defeating Colress in a post-game rematch aboard the Plasma Frigate docked at P2 Laboratory!
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — KYUREM (Lv. 70 in Giant Chasm Post-Game): Catch rate 3, required to unlock the DNA Splicers and fuse Black Kyurem (Note: Zekrom at Dragonspiral Tower has an easy catch rate of 45, and Black Kyurem during the story cannot be caught!).
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Latios (Lv. 68 in Dreamyard), Cresselia (Marvelous Bridge), or Regigigas (Twist Mountain).
Black 2.prerequisites: Reach Mistralton City (1st) / Post-Game Colress Rematch (2nd)

White 2.location: Mistralton City (Prof. Juniper) + Plasma Frigate (Colress) — Target: Kyurem & Latias
White 2.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET (2 MASTER BALLS!): First from Professor Juniper in Mistralton City; second from defeating Colress post-game on the Plasma Frigate at Route 17/P2 Lab.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — KYUREM (Lv. 70 in Giant Chasm Post-Game): Catch rate 3, unlocks the DNA Splicers to fuse White Kyurem with Reshiram.
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Latias (Lv. 68 in Dreamyard), Cresselia (Marvelous Bridge), or Heatran (Reversal Mountain).
White 2.prerequisites: Reach Mistralton City (1st) / Post-Game Colress Rematch (2nd)

X.location: Poké Ball Factory (Laverre City) — Target: Mewtwo (Unknown Dungeon)
X.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: After earning the 6th Badge (Fairy Badge from Valerie in Laverre City), infiltrate the Poké Ball Factory north of town, defeat Team Flare Admin Celosia & Bryony, and choose either balloon handed by the Factory President—he gives you BOTH the Master Ball and the Big Nugget!
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — MEWTWO (Lv. 70, Unknown Dungeon in Pokémon Village): Catch rate 3, holds Mewtwonite X, and spams Recover, Psychic, Aura Sphere, and Barrier. ⚠️ DO NOT use on Xerneas (easy catch rate 45) or the roaming Kanto Bird (which flees before you can act 11 times, then sits stationary at Sea Spirit's Den)!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Zygarde (Lv. 70 in Terminus Cave) or Stationary Articuno/Zapdos/Moltres at Sea Spirit's Den.
X.prerequisites: 6th Gym Badge & Clear Laverre Poké Ball Factory

Y.location: Poké Ball Factory (Laverre City) — Target: Mewtwo (Unknown Dungeon)
Y.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Clear Team Flare out of the Poké Ball Factory in Laverre City after earning the 6th Badge; the President awards you the Master Ball.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — MEWTWO (Lv. 70, Unknown Dungeon in Pokémon Village): Catch rate 3, holds Mewtwonite Y, and heals with Recover. ⚠️ Never waste on Yveltal (catch rate 45)!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Zygarde (Lv. 70 in Terminus Cave) or Stationary Kanto Bird at Sea Spirit's Den.
Y.prerequisites: 6th Gym Badge & Clear Laverre Poké Ball Factory

Omega Ruby.location: Team Magma Hideout (Lilycove City) — Target: Deoxys (Delta Episode Space Battle)
Omega Ruby.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Enter the Team Magma Hideout in Lilycove City and navigate the warp pad room in Maxie's office to pick up the Master Ball among the Electrodes.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — DEOXYS (Lv. 80 in Space at the climax of the Delta Episode): Right after catching Lv. 70 Rayquaza at Sky Pillar (which has a boosted story catch rate of 45), you immediately fly into space and battle Lv. 80 Deoxys (catch rate 3, knows Recover and Psycho Boost) with NO opportunity to save in between! Throwing the Master Ball at Deoxys on Turn 1 saves you from refighting it atop Sky Pillar later.
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Primal Groudon (Cave of Origin) or Mirage Spot Legendaries (Ho-Oh, Reshiram, Cresselia, Giratina).
Omega Ruby.prerequisites: Infiltrate Lilycove Team Magma Hideout

Alpha Sapphire.location: Team Aqua Hideout (Lilycove City) — Target: Deoxys (Delta Episode Space Battle)
Alpha Sapphire.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Enter the Team Aqua Hideout in Lilycove City and solve the warp pad puzzle in Archie's room to claim the Master Ball.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — DEOXYS (Lv. 80 in Space during the Delta Episode): Battled immediately after Rayquaza with no save point in between, catch rate 3, and knows Recover. Rayquaza has a boosted story catch rate (45), so catch Rayquaza in an Ultra Ball and throw your Master Ball at Deoxys!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Primal Kyogre (Cave of Origin, knows Aqua Ring) or Mirage Spot Legendaries (Lugia, Zekrom, Kyurem).
Alpha Sapphire.prerequisites: Infiltrate Lilycove Team Aqua Hideout

Sun.location: Aether Paradise Docks (from Gladion) — Target: Tapu Lele / Tapu Fini or Necrozma
Sun.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: After defeating President Lusamine at Aether Paradise before departing for Poni Island, Gladion gives you the Master Ball at the Aether Docks.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — TAPU FINI, TAPU LELE, OR NECROZMA (Lv. 75 at Ten Carat Hill): In Original Sun/Moon, Necrozma is a rare post-game encounter at Lv. 75 with a brutal catch rate of 3, while Tapu Fini spams Aqua Ring + Nature's Madness! ⚠️ DO NOT use the Master Ball on Solgaleo (easy catch rate 45) or Ultra Beasts (Beast Balls have a 5.0x multiplier on UBs)!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Tapu Koko (Lv. 60, Ruins of Conflict — colour-matches Master Ball's purple/gold!).
Sun.prerequisites: Complete Aether Paradise Infiltration

Moon.location: Aether Paradise Docks (from Gladion) — Target: Tapu Lele / Tapu Fini or Necrozma
Moon.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Gifted by Gladion at Aether Paradise Docks after Lusamine enters the Ultra Wormhole.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — NECROZMA (Lv. 75, Ten Carat Hill) OR TAPU LELE / TAPU FINI (Lv. 60): Both have catch rate 3 and annoying recovery/terrain mechanics. ⚠️ Never waste on Lunala (catch rate 45) or Ultra Beasts (use Beast Balls)!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Tapu Bulu (Ruins of Abundance).
Moon.prerequisites: Complete Aether Paradise Infiltration

Ultra Sun.location: Aether Paradise Mansion (after Rainbow Rocket) — Target: Ultra Warp Ride Legendaries
Ultra Sun.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Team Rainbow Rocket Boss Giovanni inside Lusamine's Mansion at Aether Paradise during Episode RR.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — ULTRA WARP RIDE SHINY / BOX LEGENDARIES (Mewtwo, Rayquaza, Giratina, Groudon, Ho-Oh, Reshiram): In Ultra Sun, Necrozma's catch rate was raised to 255 (guaranteed in a regular Poké Ball!), so save your Master Ball for a Shiny or 0-PP Struggle emergency inside the Ultra Wormholes or Tapu Fini!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Blacephalon (Poni Grove — knows Mind Blown which blows itself up for 50% max HP per use!).
Ultra Sun.prerequisites: Defeat Giovanni in Episode RR at Aether Paradise

Ultra Moon.location: Aether Paradise Mansion (after Rainbow Rocket) — Target: Ultra Warp Ride Legendaries
Ultra Moon.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Rainbow Rocket Giovanni at Aether Paradise during Episode RR.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — ULTRA WARP RIDE LEGENDARIES (Mewtwo, Rayquaza, Lugia, Kyogre, Zekrom, Palkia) OR TAPU FINI: Because Necrozma has a boosted catch rate in USUM, keep your Master Ball for Ultra Wormhole Legendaries or Shiny hunting!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Stakataka (Poni Grove) or Tapu Lele (Ruins of Life).
Ultra Moon.prerequisites: Defeat Giovanni in Episode RR at Aether Paradise

Let's Go Pikachu.location: Silph Co. 11F + Cerulean Cave 2F Light Spots — Target: Mewtwo or Shiny / Roaming Bird
Let's Go Pikachu.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: First Master Ball is given by the Silph Co. President on 11F after beating Giovanni. PLUS, additional Master Balls can be farmed infinitely post-game as rare sparkling floor spawns on the light spots of Cerulean Cave 2F!
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — MEWTWO (Lv. 70, Cerulean Cave B1F) OR WILD SHINY / ROAMING LEGENDARY BIRD: Mewtwo has a 5-minute battle timer and recovers HP. If you catch Mewtwo in Premier/Ultra Balls, keep a Master Ball ready in case a Shiny Pokémon or wild sky-spawning Articuno/Zapdos/Moltres performs its runaway animation!
Let's Go Pikachu.prerequisites: Defeat Giovanni at Silph Co. 11F

Let's Go Eevee.location: Silph Co. 11F + Cerulean Cave 2F Light Spots — Target: Mewtwo or Shiny / Roaming Bird
Let's Go Eevee.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Given by the Silph Co. President on 11F in Saffron City, and farmable post-game on the glowing crystal floor spots of Cerulean Cave 2F.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — MEWTWO (Lv. 70, Cerulean Cave B1F) OR SHINY FAIL-SAFE: Skips the capture ring completely with an unmissable cutscene!
Let's Go Eevee.prerequisites: Defeat Giovanni at Silph Co. 11F

Sword.location: Postwick (Prof. Magnolia) + Freezington (Peony) — Target: Calyrex, Galarian Birds, or Shiny G-Max
Sword.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET (2 MASTER BALLS!): First Master Ball is gifted by Professor Magnolia inside your house in Postwick right after defeating Champion Leon. Second Master Ball is given by Peony in Freezington when starting The Crown Tundra DLC!
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — CALYREX (Lv. 80 at Crown Shrine) OR GALARIAN ARTICUNO / ZAPDOS / MOLTRES: Calyrex has a catch rate of 3, hits like a truck in Glastrier/Spectrier form, and requires sitting through a long cutscene on every reset. Galarian Articuno (Hail damage in Crown Tundra) and Galarian Moltres/Zapdos also have catch rate 3. ⚠️ DO NOT use on Eternatus (100% guaranteed catch in any ball) or Dynamax Adventure Legendaries (100% guaranteed catch in the Max Lair)!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Non-event Shiny Gigantamax Raid Bosses (which otherwise have a ~3–8% catch rate) or Zacian (Lv. 70, Energy Plant).
Sword.prerequisites: Become Galar Champion (1st) / Enter Crown Tundra (2nd)

Shield.location: Postwick (Prof. Magnolia) + Freezington (Peony) — Target: Calyrex, Galarian Birds, or Shiny G-Max
Shield.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET (2 MASTER BALLS!): First from Professor Magnolia in Postwick after beating Leon; second from Peony in Freezington upon starting the Crown Tundra DLC.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — CALYREX (Lv. 80, Crown Shrine) OR GALARIAN BIRDS: Calyrex (Shadow/Ice Rider) has catch rate 3 and cannot be caught in Dynamax Adventures (where catches are 100% guaranteed). ⚠️ Never waste a Master Ball on Eternatus or Max Lair bosses!
3. RUNNER-UP TARGET: Shiny Gigantamax Raid Bosses or Zamazenta (Lv. 70, Energy Plant).
Shield.prerequisites: Become Galar Champion (1st) / Enter Crown Tundra (2nd)

Brilliant Diamond.location: Team Galactic HQ (Veilstone City) — Target: Roaming Mesprit/Cresselia or Ramanas Park Arceus
Brilliant Diamond.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Cyrus inside Team Galactic HQ in Veilstone City after the 7th Badge.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — ROAMING MESPRIT / CRESSELIA (Lv. 50) OR RAMANAS PARK LEGENDARIES / ARCEUS (Lv. 80): Mesprit and Cresselia roam Sinnoh and flee on Turn 1. If you have a completed Legends: Arceus save file, you unlock the Azure Flute in your bedroom to battle Lv. 80 Arceus at Spear Pillar (catch rate 3, knows Healing Wish which causes it to faint itself when out of attacking PP!).
Brilliant Diamond.prerequisites: 7 Gym Badges & Defeat Cyrus at Veilstone Galactic HQ

Shining Pearl.location: Team Galactic HQ (Veilstone City) — Target: Roaming Mesprit/Cresselia or Ramanas Park Arceus
Shining Pearl.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Defeat Cyrus inside Team Galactic HQ in Veilstone City after earning 7 Badges.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — ROAMING MESPRIT / CRESSELIA (Lv. 50) OR HALL OF ORIGIN ARCEUS (Lv. 80): Save your Master Ball for Sinnoh's two roamers or Lv. 80 Arceus at Spear Pillar!
Shining Pearl.prerequisites: 7 Gym Badges & Defeat Cyrus at Veilstone Galactic HQ

Legends: Arceus.location: Temple of Sinnoh (Origin Ball) — Target: Origin Forme Dialga / Palkia
Legends: Arceus.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Because Legends: Arceus takes place in ancient Hisui before Silph Co. invented the modern Master Ball, you instead craft the one-of-a-kind ORIGIN BALL at the Temple of Sinnoh using the Red Chain fragments and Origin Ore from Primeval Grotto!
2. #1 TARGET — ORIGIN FORME DIALGA OR PALKIA (Lv. 65 at Temple of Sinnoh): The Origin Ball has a 100% guaranteed capture rate during the climax boss battle.
3. HARDEST OVERWORLD CATCH IN HISUI — ENAMORUS (Crimson Mirelands Scarlet Bog): Bring Stealth Spray, Smoke Bombs, Sticky Globs (stun in 4 hits), and Feather/Jet Balls to break Enamorus's tornado shield!
Legends: Arceus.prerequisites: Main Mission 17: Atop Mount Coronet (Origin Ore)

Scarlet.location: Naranja Academy Director's Office (Mesagoza) — Target: Second Koraidon, Terapagos, or Chien-Pao
Scarlet.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Automatically gifted by Director Clavell in Naranja Academy after viewing the credits of 'The Way Home'. (2nd Master Ball: Register 200 Blueberry Pokédex species in The Indigo Disk DLC or print at the Item Printer in the League Club Room!).
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — SECOND KORAIDON (Lv. 72, Zero Lab Bottom Ramp) OR FOUR TREASURES OF RUIN (Chien-Pao, Chi-Yu, Ting-Lu, Wo-Chien): The aggressive Koraidon at the bottom of Area Zero is Lv. 72 with catch rate 3 and high-power Fighting/Dragon moves. In the DLC, Fezandipiti, Munkidori, Okidogi, Raging Bolt, and Gouging Fire also have low catch rates (Terapagos and Ogerpon are 100% guaranteed catches during their story battles, so do NOT waste a Master Ball on them!).
Scarlet.prerequisites: Complete 'The Way Home' Storyline

Violet.location: Uva Academy Director's Office (Mesagoza) — Target: Second Miraidon, Chien-Pao, or Iron Crown
Violet.instructions:
1. HOW TO GET: Gifted by Director Clavell in Uva Academy after completing 'The Way Home'. Additional Master Balls can be earned via the Blueberry Pokédex (200 caught) and the League Club Item Printer.
2. #1 MASTER BALL TARGET — SECOND MIRAIDON (Lv. 72, Zero Lab Bottom Ramp), TREASURES OF RUIN, OR IRON CROWN / IRON BOULDER: Miraidon's purple-and-neon color scheme and 'M' emblem match the Master Ball's design, and it sits at Lv. 72 with catch rate 3. ⚠️ Do NOT use the Master Ball on Ogerpon or Terapagos—both are 100% guaranteed story catches in any decorative ball!

quick_ball.name: Quick Ball (5.0x Turn 1 Instant Catch Rate)
quick_ball.description: The single best Poké-dex completion ball in the series: provides a massive 5.0x catch rate multiplier (4.0x in Gen 4) when thrown on the very first turn of a wild encounter!
quick_ball.generalLocation: Pastoria & Celestic Marts (Sinnoh), Goldenrod/Saffron (HGSS), Opelucid (Unova), Lumiose (Kalos), Route 8 (Alola), Wyndon (Galar), Mesagoza (Paldea)
quick_ball.generalInstructions: ALWAYS throw a Quick Ball on Turn 1 before attacking! At 5.0x catch rate (2.5x stronger than an Ultra Ball), it catches most standard wild Pokémon instantly at 100% HP. After Turn 1, its multiplier drops to 1.0x.

timer_ball.name: Timer Ball (Up to 4.0x Long Battle Catch Rate)

timer_ball.generalLocation: Rustboro City (Hoenn), Veilstone Dept. Store (Sinnoh), Goldenrod/Two Island (FRLG/HGSS), Opelucid (Unova), Lumiose (Kalos), Route 8 (Alola), Hammerlocke (Galar), All Marts (Paldea)
